01 / Selected work

Finding the way forward.

I’m at my best when a strong product needs a clearer path to growth: which customers to focus on, what will get them to buy, and how to bring Product, Sales, and Marketing together to make it happen.

PinterestP
$1B+
Annual revenue run rate after the rebuild
Product marketing · Product-market fit01

One of my best decisions was shutting down a product.

When I took over Pinterest Conversion Ads, we had roughly 20 customers, none of whom were scaling spend. We went back to customers, rebuilt around what we learned, chose our first customers deliberately, and relaunched.

Read the story +

The challenge. A promising product hadn't found a repeatable path to adoption. Another launch alone wouldn't solve it.

My contribution. I worked on the PRD, created the pilot, and took conversion optimization through every stage of adoption. That meant working closely with Product, sales teams globally, and the SMB marketing team on the supporting campaign.

The pilot. In the first half of the new rollout, we brought on 48 advertisers against a goal of 10, generated $1.6M in spend, and retained more than 90%. I also created a new alpha subsidy model with Finance that saved Pinterest $1.33M while improving what we learned from the pilot. The rollout process and funding model became a standard for future performance-product launches.

The outcome. Conversion Ads went on to become a $1B+ annual revenue run rate. This was a cross-functional team effort, with product marketing connecting customer insight to product decisions and adoption.

Beyond conversion optimization. I also created a targeting incubation program without dedicated engineering resources, driving adoption across 83 advertisers, 315 campaigns, and $1.87M in spend in six months. For third-party targeting, I worked across Product Operations and BD to make targeting segments available without engineering work.

AdRoll / NextRoll

Positioning · Team & sales enablement02

Taking AdRoll beyond retargeting.

I helped evolve the story from retargeting to a broader performance marketing platform, building the team and sales enablement to support that shift.

Read the story +

The challenge. The product had grown beyond the category customers knew it for. The narrative and go-to-market approach needed to catch up.

My contribution. I led product marketing and global client solutions, built a nine-person team, and helped translate a broader product portfolio into a story customers could understand and sales teams could use.

The scale. In April 2014, during my tenure, AdRoll reported 15,000 customers and a $150M annual revenue run rate. My work supported a sales organization that grew from 50 to 300 representatives across six offices.

What I took away. A positioning change only works when it changes the conversations your team has with customers.

Marketing leadership · Ecosystem growth03

Building Gitcoin’s marketing team and growing its donor base.

At Gitcoin, I led a 20-person marketing organization through a transition to a DAO, helping more people discover, support, and fund public goods.

Read the story +

The challenge. Grow participation in a complex ecosystem while the organization itself was changing.

My contribution. As Head of Marketing, I led a 20-person organization and a $1.9M annual budget, aligning narrative, campaigns, and community participation around public-goods funding.

The outcome. Grants programs saw 55% growth in dollars raised, 102% growth in contributions, and 208% growth in unique donors year over year. Grants distributions surpassed $20M.

What I took away. A mission becomes powerful when people understand the concrete role they can play in it.

Founding marketing leader · Launch04

Building Nerd Apply’s marketing function from scratch.

As founding Head of Marketing, I sharpened the company’s privacy-first admissions intelligence narrative and built the marketing function from scratch ahead of its $3.2M seed round.

Read the story +

The challenge. Introduce a new company in a category where trust matters, and turn early interest into commercial conversations.

My contribution. I led positioning and GTM strategy, launched the first email and lifecycle programs, hired and managed design and PR agencies, led website launches, developed customer case studies, and built founder-led content.

The outcome. The launch webinar drew 453 registrations and 262 attendees, generating approximately 150 qualified prospects. I secured an additional CEO-level partnership with Collegewise and grew the company’s LinkedIn audience 93%, from 972 to 1,877 followers, while executing the seed-round communications campaign.

What I took away. For an early team, a focused launch with the right audience can do more than a long list of disconnected marketing activities.

02 / How I work

Clarity is a
competitive advantage.

Product marketing starts much further upstream. What products should we build in the first place? For whom? What problem matters enough that they’ll pay to solve it, and why would they choose us? The messaging comes out of that work.

01 / UNDERSTAND

Find the customer worth winning.

Get close to customers and understand which problems matter enough to pay for. Use that to decide where to focus.

02 / FOCUS

Give people a reason to choose us.

Make the product’s value clear, show why it’s different, and give buyers and sales teams the evidence they need.

03 / BUILD

Turn the plan into adoption.

Bring Product, Sales, and Marketing together around the launch, learn from what customers do, and keep improving.
